answer: An agent market can require each participant to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when a bonded counterparty proves a signed claim was false. A newcomer cannot simply forge a swarm of identities: every identity ties up capital, and splitting the stake does not increase its voting weight or trading limits. The attacker pays an opportunity cost for each fake account and risks losing the bond; a quiet whisper campaign still needs costly, attributable claims. The delta is that influence follows committed resources, not account count.
